algorithms.html: A DID resolver implements the following DID resolution algorithm.

steps.html: Validate that the input DID conforms to the did rule of the DID Syntax. If not, the DID resolver MUST return the following result:
didResolutionMetadata: error object with type set to https://www.w3.org/ns/did#INVALID_DID
didDocument: null
didDocumentMetadata: «[ ]»
Determine whether the DID method of the input DID is supported by the DID resolver that implements this algorithm. If not, the DID resolver MUST return the following result:
didResolutionMetadata: error object with type set to https://www.w3.org/ns/did#METHOD_NOT_SUPPORTED
didDocument: null
didDocumentMetadata: «[ ]»
Determine whether the input DID resolution options are supported by the DID resolver that implements this algorithm. If not, the DID resolver MUST return the following result:
didResolutionMetadata: error object with type set to https://www.w3.org/ns/did#FEATURE_NOT_SUPPORTED
didDocument: null
didDocumentMetadata: «[ ]»
Determine whether the input DID resolution options are valid. If not, the DID resolver MUST return the following result:
didResolutionMetadata: error object with type set to https://www.w3.org/ns/did#INVALID_OPTIONS
didDocument: null
didDocumentMetadata: «[ ]»
Obtain the DID document for the input DID by executing the Resolve operation, as defined by the input DID method:
If the input DID does not exist, return the following result:
didResolutionMetadata: error object with type set to https://www.w3.org/ns/did#NOT_FOUND
didDocument: null
didDocumentMetadata: «[ ]»
If the input DID has been deactivated, return the following result:
didResolutionMetadata: «[ ... ]»
didDocument: null
didDocumentMetadata: «[ "deactivated" → true, ... ]»
Otherwise, the result of the Resolve operation is called the output DID document. This result MUST be represented in a conformant representation.
Return the following result:
didResolutionMetadata: «[ "contentType" → output DID document media type, ... ]»
didDocument: output DID document
didDocumentMetadata: «[ ... ]»

algorithms.html: If the DID resolver encounters any unexpected errors during the execution of the DID Resolution algorithm, it MUST return the following result:

steps.html: didResolutionMetadata: error object with type set to https://www.w3.org/ns/did#INTERNAL_ERROR
didDocument: null
didDocumentMetadata: «[ ]»
Prepare for Resolution
Resolve the DID
Determine Handling Strategy
Invoke the Handler
Use the Handler Result

Validate that the input DID URL conforms to the did-url rule of the DID URL Syntax. If not, the DID-enabled application MUST end DID URL processing, indicating a failure due to an https://www.w3.org/ns/did#INVALID_DID_URL
Select a resolver that is capable of handling the DID's method, using the resolvers that the DID URL User has set for that method (see 5. DID URL Dereferencing).
Extract the DID from the DID URL, e.g., the DID URL did:ex:abc#key-1 contains the DID did:ex:abc.

Prepare DID resolution options. These may be promoted from DID URL query parameters or determined by the business rules of the context in which the DID URL is being dereferenced. It is the business context in which the DID-enabled application is executing the algorithm that determines whether or not any given query parameter should be promoted to a resolution option. See the resolving algorithm for details about resolution options and their meaning.
Call the resolve function on the selected resolver, passing the prepared resolution options and the DID, to obtain the authoritative DID document for the input DID URL.

Interpret the response to resolve to consider any errors or warnings. If appropriate, return without further processing and raise a DEREFERENCING_ERROR_RESOLUTION_ERROR that includes the error returned from the Resolve Operation. Otherwise, continue processing if the response provided enough information to do so.

Repeat as necessary until the final resolution result is returned. In cases when the initial result from resolution is incomplete or fails, the DID-enabled application may be able to adjust the resolution parameters and try again, based on the context in which dereferencing is occurring. For example, a resolver might require more input, or the DID-enabled application might heuristically attempt alternate resolver options to find a more appropriate DID document, such as requesting a version of the DID document from a particular point in time.

algorithms.html: Using the result from resolution, execute the following steps starting with the Services Step until a handling strategy is determined. End processing as soon as a strategy is set.

steps.html:
Services Step

If the DID URL does not contain a service DID parameter, continue with the PathHandlers Step. If it contains more than one service parameter, raise an error DEREFERENCING_ERROR_MULTIPLE_SERVICE_PARAMETERS and continue to the Default DID Document Step. Otherwise, use the Service Selection Algorithm to select a service. If that algorithm raises an error, continue to the Default DID Document Step. If one of the selected service's types, other than PathHandler, defines a handling strategy, set the strategy to that strategy. Otherwise, set the strategy to the Default Service Handler strategy.

PathHandlers Step

If the DID URL contains a non-empty path part, then use the PathHandler Path Matching Algorithm to select a path handler object. If no path handler objects are selected, continue to the Document Properties step. If there are multiple handler objects selected, raise an error DEREFERENCING_ERROR_MULTIPLE_MATCHING_PATH_HANDLERS and continue to the Default DID Document Step. If a secondary type of the selected object (a type other than PathHandler) defines a handling strategy, set the strategy to that strategy. Otherwise, if the DID document property that contains the selected object defines a handling strategy for it, set the strategy to that strategy. For an object in the service property, that is the Default Service Handler strategy. Otherwise, raise an error DEREFERENCING_ERROR_PATH_HANDLER_HANDLER_NOT_DEFINED and continue to the Default DID Document Step.

Document Properties Step

If the DID document contains any properties known to define a handler strategy, check whether any of those properties apply to the DID URL. If not, continue with the Method-Specific Step. If the DID document contains multiple properties that apply to the DID URL, raise an error DEREFERENCING_ERROR_MULTIPLE_DOCUMENT_PROPERTIES and continue to the Default DID Document Step. If the DID document contains a single property with a known handler strategy that applies to the DID URL, set the strategy to the strategy defined by that property. Otherwise, continue to the Method-Specific Step.

Method-Specific Step

If the DID method defines a method-specific handler strategy, check whether that handler applies to the DID URL. If it does, set the handler strategy to that specified by the DID method. If there is no applicable method-specific handler strategy, continue with the Query Parameters Step.

Query Parameters Step

If there are query parameters that require a specific handling strategy, check to see if there are more than one. If there are, then raise an error DEREFERENCING_ERROR_MULTIPLE_QUERY_PARAMETERS and continue to the Default DID Document Step. If there is only one such query parameter, set the strategy to that defined by the query parameter specification. Otherwise, continue with the Metadata Step.

Not all query parameters will change the handling strategy. For example, versionTime and versionId affect the resolution result when they are passed as resolution options (see 5.1.1 Prepare for Resolution), but do not change the handling strategy. Similarly, strategy-independent parameters do not select a handling strategy, but can be applied by the handler once one is chosen (see 5.1.4 Invoke the Handler).

Metadata Step

If either the DID resolution metadata or DID document metadata contain any properties known to define a handler strategy, check to see if any of those properties apply to the DID URL. If there is only one such property, set the strategy to the strategy defined by that property. If there are multiple applicable properties, raise an error DEREFERENCING_ERROR_MULTIPLE_METADATA_PROPERTIES and continue to the Default DID Document Step. Otherwise, continue to Default DID Document Step.
Default DID Document Step If no other handler strategy has been determined, set the strategy to Return DID Document.

Execute the determined handler strategy using a handler that implements that strategy. If the DID-enabled application does not have a handler that implements the determined strategy, stop processing and raise an error DEREFERENCING_ERROR_HANDLER_NOT_FOUND.

The handler is provided with the input DID URL (including its path, query, and fragment components), the DID resolution result, and, where applicable, the object from which the handling strategy was determined.

In addition to any query parameters defined by the specification for the determined handling strategy, a handler MAY process strategy-independent parameters: DID URL query parameters that are not tied to any one handling strategy, and that are defined in 3. DID Parameters, by a DID parameter extension, or by the DID method. A handler MUST ignore query parameters it does not support, and MAY report a warning identifying them.

algorithms.html: When a DID URL contains a service parameter use the following algorithm to determine which service should be used for dereferencing the DID URL.

steps.html: Select the service from the DID document whose id property has a fragment (without the leading #) that exactly matches the value of the service DID query parameter. The id property can be an absolute DID URL or a relative reference containing only a fragment (e.g., #files).
If no service matches, raise an error DEREFERENCING_ERROR_SERVICE_NOT_FOUND; no service is selected.
If more than one service matches, raise an error DEREFERENCING_ERROR_MULTIPLE_MATCHING_SERVICES; no service is selected.
If a single service matches, that service is selected.
Return the selected service, or the error raised, to the Services Step.

algorithms.html: Consider the following DID URL and DID Document section:

steps.html:
Select Service Endpoint If serviceEndpoint is a single value, use it. If serviceEndpoint is instead an array, randomly pick one of the service's serviceEndpoint values as a starting point. Since each value in the array is expected to resolve to the same set of resources (and any given DID URL triggering that service will retrieve the same resource from any of the endpoints), successfully dereferencing any one of them is sufficient. Implementations MUST keep track of each endpoint as it is attempted, so that each is exercised until either a successful result is returned or the complete set of endpoints has been attempted. In other words raise a failure error DEREFERENCING_ERROR_NO_SERVICE_ENDPOINTS_SUCCEED only after all of the endpoints fail. 
serviceEndpoint = "https://example.com/didimages/"

Determine Resource Path Construct the resource path by extracting the non-matching part of the DID URL and appending it to the path of the serviceEndpoint. First extract the pathExtension: the part of the DID URL path that remains after removing the leading match with the service's path value, as determined by the PathHandler Path Matching Algorithm. If the service was selected by the service DID parameter rather than by that algorithm, apply the same matching rule to the selected service's path value. If the service has no path property, treat its value as "/". If the DID URL has an empty path, the pathExtension is empty. If the DID URL has a non-empty path that does not begin with the service's path value, stop processing and raise an error DEREFERENCING_ERROR_SERVICE_PATH_MISMATCH. The pathExtension in the above example is "image.png", after stripping the service's path value of "/" from the path part of the DID URL /image.png. 
pathExtension = "image.png";
Append the pathExtension to the path part of the serviceEndpoint to define the resourcePath. 
resourcePath = /didimages/image.png

Normalize Path Normalize the resourcePath to create a normalizedResourcePath by removing dot segments, as defined in RFC3986 Section 5.2.4. Then test whether the leftmost characters of the normalizedResourcePath match the path part of the serviceEndpoint. If they do not match, raise an error DEREFERENCING_ERROR_PATH_NORMALIZATION_ERROR.

Construct Resource URL Replace the path part of the selected serviceEndpoint with the normalizedResourcePath, leaving all other parts of the serviceEndpoint URL unchanged. The result is the resource URL. 
resource URL = https://example.com/didimages/image.png

The query parameters and fragment of the DID URL are not copied to the resource URL. A query parameter changes the resource URL only when it is applied in the Apply Strategy-Independent Parameters step. The handler applies the fragment, if any, to the retrieved resource, as described in 5.1.5 Use the Handler Result.

Apply Strategy-Independent Parameters If the DID URL contains strategy-independent parameters that the DID-enabled application supports and that are defined, in 3. DID Parameters, by a DID parameter extension, or by the DID method, to modify the resource URL, apply them in the order defined by their specifications. Any resulting resource URL MUST again satisfy the check in the Normalize Path step.
Dereference Resource URL Dereference the resulting resource URL according to its scheme. For example, for an https URL, perform a GET operation on that URL.

algorithms.html: When a DID Document contains a path and one or more objects with a type of PathHandler use the following algorithm to determine which object and handler should be used for dereferencing the DID URL.

steps.html:
Of those objects with a type PathHandler, select the object whose path property has the longest complete match from the beginning of the path part of the DID URL. The entire value of the path property must be present in the path part of the DID URL.
Given the DID URL did:example:1234/image.png and the following three PathHandling objects

In this scenario, the linkedResource object with id #SecuredImage would be selected, and the handling strategy would be defined by a specification associated with the linkedResource object.

If two or more objects have the same length match, raise an error DEREFERENCING_ERROR_MULTIPLE_MATCHING_PATH_HANDLERS; no object is selected. Return the selected object, or the error raised, to the PathHandlers Step.

algorithms.html: Using this binding, the DID resolution function (see 4. DID Resolution) can be executed as follows:

steps.html: Initialize a request HTTP(S) URL with the DID resolver HTTP(S) endpoint.
For the DID resolution function:
Append the input DID to the request HTTP(S) URL.
Set the Accept HTTP request header to application/did-resolution to request a complete 7. DID Resolution Result, OR
set the Accept HTTP request header to the value of the accept resolution option to request only the didDocument value of the result.
For the HTTP(S) GET binding:
If any other resolution options than accept are provided:
The input DID MUST be URL-encoded (as specified in RFC3986 Section 2.1).
Encode all resolution options except accept as query parameters in the request HTTP(S) URL.
Execute an HTTP GET request on the request HTTP(S) URL. This invokes the DID resolution function at the remote DID resolver.
For the HTTP(S) POST binding:
If any other resolution options than accept are provided:
Encode all resolution options except accept as a JSON structure in the HTTP request's POST body.
Execute an HTTP POST request on the request HTTP(S) URL. This invokes the DID resolution function at the remote DID resolver.

If the DID resolution function returns an error metadata property in the didResolutionMetadata, then the HTTP response status code MUST correspond to the type property of the error object, according to the following table:
error type URI HTTP status code
https://www.w3.org/ns/did#INVALID_DID 400
https://www.w3.org/ns/did#INVALID_DID_URL 400
https://www.w3.org/ns/did#INVALID_OPTIONS 400
https://www.w3.org/ns/did#NOT_FOUND 404
https://www.w3.org/ns/did#REPRESENTATION_NOT_SUPPORTED 406
https://www.w3.org/ns/did#INVALID_DID_DOCUMENT 500
https://www.w3.org/ns/did#METHOD_NOT_SUPPORTED 501
https://www.w3.org/ns/did#FEATURE_NOT_SUPPORTED 501
https://www.w3.org/ns/did#INTERNAL_ERROR 500

If the type property of the error object does not appear in the table above, then the HTTP response status code is determined by the implementation.
If the DID resolution function returns a deactivated metadata property with the value true in the didDocumentMetadata:
The HTTP response status code MUST be 410, even if a step below requires a different status code.
For the DID resolution function:
If the value of the Content-Type HTTP response header is application/did-resolution:
If the function is successful, the HTTP response status code MUST be 200.
The HTTP body MUST contain a DID resolution result (see 7. DID Resolution Result) that is the result of the DID resolution function.
Otherwise, if the function is successful and returns a didDocument:
The HTTP response status code MUST be 200.
The HTTP response MUST contain a Content-Type HTTP response header. Its value MUST be the value of the contentType metadata property in the didResolutionMetadata (see 4.2 DID Resolution Metadata).
The HTTP response body MUST contain the didDocument that is the result of the DID resolution function, in the representation corresponding to the Content-Type HTTP response header.
